Definition: from a compound of G3956 and G3696; full armor ("panoply"):--all (whole) armour.
BiblicalUsage: Panoplia is the full armour, the complete equipment of a soldier. A stronger man takes from the strong man all his armour wherein he trusted, and Paul commands the church to put on the whole armour of God that they may stand against the wiles of the devil.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the armour is whole or it is nothing. God does not hand out a shield and forget the sword, and the stand comes from wearing all of it.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
